name: Stahl-Koenig Industries IronGuard Assault Kit
description: Brutalist matte-black and industrial rust-red composite plate armor over reinforced ballistic fatigues, bearing Stahl-Koenig's angular SK-anvil logo embossed in iron-grey on the chest and helmet crest. The helmet is a full-skull hard shell with integrated thermal overlay and blast-rated visor, built to survive foundry-floor conditions as readily as a firefight. Load-bearing rig is heavy-duty modular steel-frame webbing carrying breaching tools, suppression rounds, and a corded industrial torch. Boots are foundry-grade magnesium-alloy reinforced, rated for molten splash and ballistic fragmentation.
functionality: Blast and fragmentation resistance, thermal overlay HUD, foundry-rated heat protection, and heavy breaching equipment compatibility.
what_it_says: Stahl-Koenig doesn't send diplomats — they send infrastructure.
story_hooks: An IronGuard unit has been stationed inside a facility that officially shut down three years ago — and they're still receiving active supply drops.
The embossed SK-anvil logo on one operative's chest plate has been ground off and spray-painted over — someone is running a ghost unit.

physical_description.visual_profile: Imposing brutalist silhouette dominated by angular composite plating. Heavy, architectural presence suggesting industrial utility crossed with tactical combat function. Wearer appears broadened and reinforced, almost mechanized.
physical_description.fit: Rigid compression fit over a structured combat-grade fatigues base. Plates are mounted externally on a load-bearing skeleton, creating distinct layering. Deliberate unyielding stance—designed for functionality, not comfort.
physical_description.primary_material: Composite plate armor (matte-black polymer-ceramic blend) layered over ballistic weave fatigues. Steel-frame modular webbing. Magnesium-alloy reinforced foundry-grade boots. Polymer-graphite helmet shell.
physical_description.texture: Matte non-reflective surfaces with industrial texture. Armor plates show subtle stippling and slight corrosion patina. Webbing has dense, rigid weave. Visor is hard-polished and slightly reflective. Heavy, tactile, unforgiving.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary matte black with industrial rust-red accent plating. Iron-grey embossed SK-anvil logo on chest and helmet crest. Dark olive fatigues visible at joints and beneath armor.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty friction-fit modular connections. Ballistic fatigues feature reinforced magnetic snap closures. Helmet locks via pressure-fit collar mechanism. Load-bearing webbing uses mil-spec buckles and carabiners.
distinctive_features: Full-skull blast-rated helmet with integrated thermal overlay and hard visor
Angular SK-anvil logo embossed in iron-grey on chest plate and helmet crest
Reinforced composite plating with industrial stipple finish
Integrated thermal imaging overlay in visor
Modular attachment points for breaching tools and suppression rounds
Corded industrial torch mount on webbing
Visible ballistic fragmentation rating markings on plates
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2 corporate military—high-end tactical equipment manufactured by major defense contractor. Price point signals corpo security or PMC deployment.
physical_description.cultural_context: Stahl-Koenig corporate security, PMC operator, or elite industrial-site enforcement. Wearer signals allegiance to manufacturing bloc and willingness for direct combat engagement. Heavy gear = serious threat.
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-fresh or showing minimal combat scuffing. Matte black remains pristine; rust-red accents may show light oxidation from foundry conditions. Equipment is routinely maintained and replaced under Stahl-Koenig service contracts.

image_prompt: A heavily armored corpo security operator in full Stahl-Koenig IronGuard Assault Kit standing in industrial three-quarter profile. Matte-black composite plate armor dominates the frame, with rust-red accent plating catching moody amber-blue neon light. Full-skull helmet with thermal visor overlay glows faintly. Steel-frame load-bearing webbing stretches across chest and shoulders, carrying tools and ordnance. Magnesium-alloy foundry boots grip a grated metal floor. Dark blue-grey fatigues visible at joints and neck. SK-anvil logo embossed in iron-grey catches light. Backdrop is brutalist concrete foundry interior with orange furnace glow and cyan-tinted skylights. Cinematic rim lighting emphasizes angular armor plates and tactical geometry. Gritty, industrial, utterly impassive. Neo-noir military aesthetic. --ar 2:3 --v 6
